Platform

Airtable for Regulated Organisations

Airtable is often described as a database, which undersells it and misleads buyers in regulated environments. In our work it functions as a workflow platform, an operational control layer, a case management environment and a governance record, provided it is designed and governed with the discipline a regulated process requires.

Positioning

Not a database. An operational control platform.

Airtable is a strong place to run the workflow and hold the operational record around regulated processes. It should not be asked to be the bank’s ledger, and we will say so during discovery if your design asks it to be.

Workflow platform

Stages, ownership, routing and service levels for operational processes, with automations that move work between teams.

Operational control platform

Mandatory fields, validation, role-based permissions and approval gates that enforce how work is done.

Case management platform

Linked records for alerts, cases, clients, evidence and decisions, with views tailored to each role.

Governance platform

Decision logs, control registers and action trackers that committees and auditors can interrogate.

Use cases

Where regulated teams run work on Airtable

Alert and case queues

Structured case records with SLAs, ownership and escalation, replacing shared spreadsheets and inbox tracking.

KYC refresh management

Scheduled review cycles per customer segment, document requests, and a completion record for each refresh.

Control testing

Test plans, sampling records, results and remediation tracked against each control in the register.

Vendor due diligence

Questionnaire workflows, evidence collection and periodic review schedules for third parties.

Policy attestation

Policy versions linked to attestation campaigns, with reminders and escalation for non-responders.

Regulatory change tracking

Horizon scanning inputs, impact assessment workflows and implementation actions linked to affected controls.

Architecture

A layered design with clear system boundaries

Airtable sits in the workflow and control layer. Systems of record stay where they are, and AI services sit behind an approval gate.

Experience

  • Role-specific views
  • Forms for controlled data capture
  • Dashboards for committees

Workflow and control

  • Airtable bases with defined schemas
  • Validation, permissions and approval gates
  • Versioned automation logic

Orchestration

  • Automation platform such as Make, n8n, Zapier or Workato
  • Retry, failure and exception handling
  • Monitoring of runs and errors

AI services

  • Model APIs behind an approval gate
  • Prompt and rule versioning
  • Output logging with reviewer identity

Systems of record

  • Core banking, KYC and screening engines
  • Data warehouse for reporting
  • Document and evidence stores

Audit and assurance

  • Exported activity logs
  • Control evidence index
  • Independent testing access

AI integrations

AI that proposes inside a controlled base

  • Case narrative drafting from structured fields, with the analyst editing and approving before the record is saved
  • Document extraction into structured fields, with confidence scores and a verification queue for low-confidence items
  • Summarisation of long evidence threads for reviewers, linked back to the source messages
  • Classification and routing of incoming requests, with rules that override the model for defined categories

Workflow examples

How controlled workflows look on the platform

Screening potential match

  1. Screening tool posts a potential match via API
  2. Record created with risk category and due date
  3. Analyst disposition with mandatory rationale
  4. Second-line sample selected by rule
  5. Closed record written to audit log

Periodic KYC review

  1. Refresh schedule generates tasks by risk rating
  2. Customer document request issued through a controlled form
  3. Documents received and verified against checklist
  4. Decision approved at the level set by risk rating
  5. Next review date set automatically

Regulatory return sign-off

  1. Source data loaded and reconciled against control totals
  2. Exceptions raised to named data owners
  3. Preparer submits, reviewer approves, senior sign-off recorded
  4. Submission reference and evidence stored against the return

Governance examples

The controls that make the platform defensible

Role-based permissions with field-level restrictions on sensitive data, reviewed quarterly

Change control for automations and field definitions, with a release log and test evidence

Immutable activity history exported to a separate audit store on a schedule

Data retention rules applied by table, with deletion logged and approved

Honest boundaries

Where Airtable should not be used

We will tell you if your design asks the platform to do something it should not. That conversation protects you during supervisory review.

  • As the system of record for transactions, balances or regulatory data that other systems must treat as authoritative
  • For high-volume, low-latency processing that belongs in an engine designed for throughput
  • Where access requirements cannot be met through permissions and the data must be partitioned at a deeper level
  • Where no owner will govern the base, its automations and its change history

Questions

Airtable in regulated environments: common questions

Is Airtable acceptable for regulated data?

That depends on your data classification, your vendor due diligence and how the platform is configured. We include vendor assessment, permission design, data retention and audit export in every regulated deployment, and we document the residual risks for your risk committee.

Why not build this in a case management suite?

Sometimes you should. Where a dedicated case platform fits your process, we will recommend it. Airtable is a good choice when processes change frequently, when business teams need to maintain workflows, and when the control layer needs to be designed around your specific requirements.

Do you build Airtable bases for clients?

We design and build the workflow, control and integration layers, and we hand over the governance model so your team can operate it. We do not replace your internal capability with a permanent dependency on us.

Design the control layer before you configure the base.

We run a platform-fit review that checks data classification, permissions, audit export and ownership before anything is built.
